A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TurBLiMP and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. All 13 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2 support comparison, including matching material across relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 language models, judgments from 30 Turkish speakers, and word-order and subordination experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds SLOR correlations, surface-feature regressions, tokenizer evaluations, and an instruction-tuning comparison.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendix A retain the same manually seeded, BERTurk-augmented benchmark construction and paradigm generation. The added inflection qualifier 'when applicable' does not establish an actual procedure change.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds evaluation of tokenizer alignment on 400 morphologically segmented Turkish words across four morphological categories. This introduces a bounded word-level task alongside the unchanged sentence-acceptability benchmark, linguistic phenomena, and human-study population.

E2.justification: The 13-model comparison in Table 2 is unchanged. However, v2's Limitations adds an evaluated Gemma 3 (4B) Instruct versus base comparison, whereas v1 only explained excluding instruction-tuned variants.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation protocols with SLOR scoring, four-model regressions controlling sentence-length and cue-word subword-count differences, and tokenizer evaluation using edit distance, undersegmentation, oversegmentation, and exact matches. The original benchmark scoring and human-survey procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests whether model–human correlations depend on the scoring metric. Appendix E adds surface-confound analyses and a morphological-alignment follow-up investigating tokenizer explanations. These substantially extend the retained word-order and subordination robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix E adds linear-regression estimation, standardized coefficients, R-squared reporting, and error bars in Figure 4, although the bars' statistical meaning is unspecified. Existing standard-error and Pearson-significance reporting remains; no increased run or seed count is documented.

E6.justification: Original results in Tables 2–9 are retained. New results include SLOR correlations, with only BERTurk significant at r = 0.557 and p = 0.0251; regression R-squared values of 0.082–0.185; and tokenizer-alignment scores in Table 11. Gemma 3 (4B) Instruct accuracy is additionally reported as 4.4% lower than its base variant. These are added findings, not revised main-benchmark performance.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised. The new statistics and segmentation measures are empirical evaluation tools, and the expanded linguistic example is explanatory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the benchmark contribution, monolingual-model findings, model–human discrepancies, and sensitivity to word order and subordination. The new analyses support these claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive explanations of opposing sentence-length effects in autoregressive and masked models, limited explanatory power of surface features, and why tokenizer alignment alone cannot explain performance. The instruction-tuning exclusion also gains an empirical rationale beyond v1's assumption.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly discloses recruitment through the authors' close networks. Appendix E documents the morphological pipeline, four word categories, and 100 items per category for the new tokenizer dataset. Existing model details and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Chirkova and Nikoulina, Damerau, Goldman et al., and Pauls and Klein. It also distinguishes its full-morpheme-boundary evaluation from Arnett and Bergen's stem-versus-suffix assessment. The main benchmark positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include a glossed subordination example, clearer normalization explanations, an expanded limitations paragraph, acknowledgments, and new appendices D–E, without extensive rewriting of existing sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4 and Tables 10–11, expands Table 3's caption to explain units and score differences, and relocates existing displays. The original tables, plots, and overall two-column design are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The SLOR check directly addresses a scoring-artifact concern, while Appendix E supplies useful evidence about length and tokenization biases, strengthening interpretation of the benchmark. The gains are bounded: SLOR frequency estimation and Figure 4's error bars remain underdocumented, and the new regressions do not establish that confounding is eliminated.
